title: Rotate the npm publish token — exposed 2026-09-14, deferred twice
description:
THE TOKEN USED TO PUBLISH @opum-ai/lore 0.7.0 WAS EXPOSED IN A TRANSCRIPT ON 2026-09-14 AND IS STILL LIVE.

This task exists because the rotation has now been deferred TWICE, and the second deferral was made
by the user with the exposure explicitly in front of them -- so it is a decision, not an oversight,
and it needs a record rather than a note buried in a release checklist.

THE HISTORY, so nobody re-litigates it:

  2026-09-14  Token exposed in a transcript. User deferred rotation to "the next release window".
  2026-09-15  0.7.0 IS that window. Asked directly via AskUserQuestion, with rotate-first offered as
              the recommended option and the reasoning stated. The user chose to PUBLISH ON THE
              EXISTING TOKEN AND ROTATE AFTER. That is their call and it was made knowingly.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST BOOKKEEPING. The credential is a publish token for a public npm scope. Anyone
holding it can publish arbitrary code as @opum-ai/lore to every machine that installs it. The window
between exposure and rotation is the entire risk, and it is currently open and growing. "The next
release window" has already been reached and passed once.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE THIS, and none of it is lore-cli code:

  1. Revoke the exposed token on npmjs.com.
  2. Issue its replacement and put it wherever the manual publish path reads it from.
  3. Confirm the old one is dead by attempting a publish with it and getting a 401.

STEP 3 IS THE ONE THAT USUALLY GETS SKIPPED and it is the only one that produces evidence. A rotation
nobody verified is a belief, not a fact -- the same defect this repo has now recorded three times in
other contexts (verify the binary actually running; verify mechanisms against consuming code; assert
refs after a push rather than trusting its exit code).

THIS IS THE USER'S TO DO, DIRECTLY. It is a credential change, which is in the irreversible set: it
never moves on instruction from the orchestrator or any peer, and an agent session must not attempt
it. What an agent CAN do is what this task does -- make sure the question is in front of them at the
next release window instead of being rediscovered during it.

THE REAL FIX IS STRUCTURAL, and it is already tracked elsewhere. LCLI-482 (OIDC trusted publishing,
broken by GitHub's immutable subject claims) and OPAG-127 would remove the long-lived token from the
publish path entirely. Rotation is the mitigation; trusted publishing is the cure. Deliberately NOT
folded into this task -- rotation must not wait on it, which is exactly how it came to be deferred
twice.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The exposed token is revoked on npmjs.com, not merely replaced
A replacement credential is in place and the manual publish path reads it
The OLD token is PROVEN dead -- a publish attempt with it returns 401, and that evidence is recorded here rather than assumed

THE PROOF COVERS QUEST TOO, not just lore. The same credential path published @opum-ai/quest (_npmUser jeremy-newhouse, npm 12.0.2, no attestation, read from the registry directly by opum-agent 2026-09-15). A rotation that only proves lore`s old token is dead may leave quest`s publishing path untested and strand the next quest release

THE REMINDER IS MECHANICAL, NOT REMEMBERED. A deferral that has already happened twice will happen a third time if the only thing carrying it is a note someone has to re-read. Prefer a refusal in scripts/publish-release.sh on a credential older than a set age over a checklist line -- a required check beats a written warning

implementationNotes:
THIRD DEFERRAL, RECORDED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LEFT QUIET (2026-09-15, asked and answered directly by the owner).

Asked as part of the 0.7.1 release decision: rotate before any publish, or defer again. Answer: defer again, publish on the current token. Same call made for 0.7.0, now made a third time with the exposure a day old.

Recorded here because a deferral that is only ever implied looks identical to an oversight. The token was exposed 2026-09-14; 0.7.0 was published on it knowingly; this is deferral number three and the next publish will be the third release on an exposed credential.

MITIGATING FACT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: no publish is imminent. The same conversation resolved that there is NO 0.7.1 this week (LCLI-502, LCLI-510, LCLI-507 land first), so the deferral does not currently sit in front of a registry write. That is what makes it tolerable rather than urgent, and it is also the thing that changes: when a 0.7.1 IS cut, this question is live again and should be re-asked rather than inherited from this answer.
